evidence.title: Archon: Quickstart; Connect a platform
evidence.finding: Archon has a product CLI and self-hosted browser console. macOS/Linux and Windows installers are documented, and Slack/Telegram/GitHub adapters are separate conversation channels. Installable CLI platforms do not establish native desktop GUIs.

evidence.title: Archon: Your agents, your subscriptions; Plugin kinds
evidence.locator: Your agents, your subscriptions; Plugin kinds
evidence.finding: Maintained provider plugins run Claude Code, Codex and Pi using their CLIs/SDKs. Community providers use a published contract; compatibility and workflow capabilities are provider-specific.

evidence.title: Archon: Your agents, your subscriptions; Quickstart
evidence.finding: Archon runs existing Claude Code, Codex and Pi accounts. The quickstart asks users to install and sign into Claude Code or Codex before setup.

evidence.title: Archon: Quickstart
evidence.finding: Users install and sign in to Claude Code or install Codex, install Archon, then run a named workflow in any git repository.

evidence.title: Archon: API Reference; Authentication
evidence.finding: Archon exposes a REST API under /api with OpenAPI 3 generation. Solo local authentication is optional; configured web auth requires a session or trusted proxy identity. The CLI controls workflow runs and approvals.

evidence.title: Archon: A reliable core; Plugin kinds
evidence.finding: Versioned plugins supply workflow packs, agent providers, forges and chat adapters through a published contract and install from GitHub; users can build their own plugins.

evidence.title: Archon: A software factory
evidence.finding: The SDLC pack takes GitHub issues through intake, build and merge queues via the forge plugin. External issues remain the durable intake objects; this is not the archived native RAG/task app.

evidence.title: Archon: Workflow language
evidence.finding: YAML workflows declare ordered or dependent agent, script, loop, wait and approval nodes, with output contracts and persisted runs. Workflow files can be edited and versioned in the project.

evidence.title: Archon: Separate governed child runs; fan_out
evidence.finding: A workflow node can launch separate child runs with their own identity, artifacts, costs and pauses. Dependencies and fan-out govern execution; max_parallel caps concurrent children rather than total work.

evidence.title: Archon: Your agents; Workflow packs
evidence.finding: Archon reuses provider project guidance and stores workflow commands and scripts beside YAML. This does not establish a shared cross-provider semantic memory store.

evidence.title: Archon: A software factory
evidence.finding: The discoveries workflow reads out-of-task findings and files them as new GitHub issues or attaches them to existing issues through the forge plugin. Native issue object parity is not asserted.

evidence.title: Archon: Workflow language; Artifact chain
evidence.finding: Workflow YAML and node outputs form persistent implementation inputs and revisioned process definitions. This is not proof of product-spec drift detection across later unrelated work.

evidence.title: Archon: fan_out; Concurrency
evidence.finding: Workflow fan-out creates concurrent governed child runs and max_parallel limits active children. Parent and child records remain inspectable.

evidence.title: Archon: A software factory
evidence.finding: The build queue claims ready issues; the merge queue processes ready PRs and returns conflicts for rework. The bundled pack binds no triggers by default.

evidence.title: Archon: Launching a separate governed run
evidence.finding: The product assistant can invoke workflows and inspect runs; workflow nodes delegate child runs with output returned to their parent, separate artifacts, pauses and cost records.

evidence.title: Archon: Start workflows from schedules and signed webhooks
evidence.locator: Start workflows from schedules and signed webhooks
evidence.finding: Native schedules, GitHub events and Standard Webhooks request governed runs with host identity, overlap policy and resource admission. The configured server or detached CLI host starts admitted work and deduplicates shared admission records.

evidence.title: Archon: Workflows and runs; Alerts
evidence.finding: Console actions include approve, reject, resume, cancel and abandon. Optional alerts announce approval/attention waits, completion, failure and cancellation.

evidence.title: Archon: Console navigation; Workflows and runs
evidence.finding: The console lists runs across projects and exposes per-run event logs, artifacts and graph context when the workflow definition is available. Fleet-navigation effort was not measured.

evidence.title: Archon: Build any factory; Quickstart
evidence.finding: Users invoke a ready workflow in natural language or edit the YAML graph to combine agent prompts, scripts, waits, loops and child workflows.

evidence.title: Archon: Deployment overview
evidence.finding: Archon can run locally for development or be deployed with Docker or on a cloud VPS for always-on operation, using SQLite by default or PostgreSQL.

evidence.title: Archon: What it looks like
evidence.finding: Repository runs receive their own Git worktree by default, permitting separate runs against the same repository.

evidence.title: Archon: How it works; Provider support; Security posture
evidence.locator: How it works; Provider support; Security posture
evidence.finding: Folder projects optionally run in Docker with read-only project root, overlay writes and approval-gated write-back. Only Claude nodes currently support this container mode; other providers fail before execution. Native overlay fallback uses CAP_SYS_ADMIN and is not hostile-agent containment.

evidence.title: Archon: Pause economics
evidence.finding: Normal container pauses stop compute; resume can restart or recreate the container from its persisted upper volume. Missing volumes fail loudly. Web/chat decisions cannot continue container execution; a same-project CLI resume is required.

evidence.title: Archon: Prerequisites; Running
evidence.finding: Container runs require Docker and a current runner image containing tools. Artifacts are retained through a dedicated writable bind; stopped containers preserve their upper volume for resume.

evidence.title: Archon: Run budgets; Retry policy
evidence.finding: Optional run budgets enforce work-unit and provider-reported USD spend ceilings before new attempts. In-flight work can overshoot spend, unknown cost fails a spend-capped run, and budgeted nested/loop shapes are rejected if unsupported.

evidence.title: Archon: Workflows and runs
evidence.finding: Run details expose event logs and artifacts; live events show governance state. Documentation describes retry and failure records but no induced worker-failure consistency test was run.

evidence.title: Archon: Cost roll-up; Reading tokens and cost
evidence.locator: Cost roll-up; Reading tokens and cost
